title: Sorrel and the Sneezing Wind
markdown:
Once upon a time, in a meadow that smelled of lavender and chamomile, Sorrel the herb seller hummed a little tune, as soft and sweet as the blossoms they nurtured. They set their baskets beside the path, fingers forever smelling faintly of those same flowers. Beside them sat Blink, a little green frog in a wonderfully wide, wonderfully soft hat that always tilted in a thoughtful way. Blink watched with dewdrop eyes and offered a quiet croak now and then, like a tiny bubble in a still pond.

They were collecting special herbs today, precious gifts for a healing class that would happen later, a class whispered to be very important for mending little worries and soothing tiny troubles. There was the sweet, cool mint, its leaves like little emerald jewels; the earthy, warming thyme, smelling of sunshine and meadows; and a special moonleaf, shimmering with a pale silvery glow, said to hold the very heart of soft moonlight. Sorrel carefully nestled each one into a woven basket, their movements slow and careful, like a lullaby sung to the flowers.

Then a peculiar puff of wind tiptoed through the market stalls. Not gusty. Whispery. Tickly. It carried a funny shimmer, like dust motes in a sunbeam. And with a surprising, utterly gentle “Achoo!”, the wind seemed to sneeze.

“Catch me if you can, but catch me kind,” said the wind, in a voice like grass.

Suddenly the air around Sorrel’s stall filled with herbs, gently floating, as if set free to explore. The mint bobbed like tiny green balloons. The thyme twirled, a miniature dance. The precious moonleaf rose higher, a pale kite. Sorrel gave a little gasp, a surprised flutter, not a scared one. Blink’s hat wobbled. The healing class would begin very soon, and the soothing herbs were dancing in the sky.

Sorrel did not tangle themselves in worry. “Oh dear,” they murmured, voice as soft as a lullaby. “We’ll have to be very careful, Blink. Very gentle indeed.” Blink croaked a knowing croak. His little froggy feet wiggled.

First the mint. Sorrel watched a cluster drift lower, tired from its skyward adventure. With a slow careful swoop they cupped their hands and caught the leaves, like catching raindrops, each one landing softly in their palm.

Second the thyme. Blink, from a nearby basket, used his long sticky tongue not to snatch but to guide a wafting sprig closer to Sorrel’s outstretched hand. A silent agreement between friends. The feathery leaves came home.

Third, and hardest, the moonleaf wanted to explore a little longer. It floated near a tall friendly sunflower, pale leaves in the warm light, a tiny silver moon in a golden halo. Sorrel took a deep calming breath, like a wave rolling slowly onto the shore.

They reached toward the sunflower. A touch as light as a butterfly’s wing encouraged the moonleaf closer. At last, with slow steady care, Sorrel collected it, glow reassuring and warm in their palm.

The wind, its achoo spent, settled among the sunflowers, no more than a polite puff that would not lift a petal. It had been caught in kindness, and so it learned to keep its sneezes small.

Blink hopped onto Sorrel’s shoulder, hat settling as if it too had travelled. The healing class was gathering, faces full of quiet waiting. Sorrel smiled, a soft warm smile. The herbs were safe, their gentle magic ready.

A little care returns what a sneeze sets free.

And their tale is still told when the festival wind grows tickly, and someone remembers to cup their hands. As the sun dipped, rose and lavender and sleepy orange, Sorrel and Blink sat together watching fireflies twinkle. The air grew cooler. A hush fell, crickets and rustling leaves. Blink yawned a big froggy yawn, hat tilting forward. Soon, tucked among lavender and chamomile, they drifted into peaceful slumber, hearts full of the day’s quiet joys, and the promise of sweet dreams.
